name: Kentucky
summary: The state seal on navy blue: a frontiersman in buckskin and a statesman in a frock coat shaking hands, with the motto 'United we stand, divided we fall', inside a wreath of goldenrod.
origin: The General Assembly adopted the flag on 26 March 1918. The seal dates from 1792, Kentucky's statehood; the motto comes from 'The Liberty Song' of 1768.

symbols.name: Two men shaking hands
symbols.meaning: Unity; commonly identified as Daniel Boone and Henry Clay, though officially they represent all frontiersmen and statesmen.

symbols.name: Goldenrod
symbols.description: A wreath of the state flower.

facts: The men are popularly identified as Daniel Boone and Henry Clay.
The motto was also used on Kentucky's earliest seal of 1792.
clues: A seal on navy blue with two men shaking hands, ringed by goldenrod.
Its motto is 'United we stand, divided we fall'.
Its two figures are often said to be a frontiersman and a famous senator.
